findings:
🟠 [d2-verdict-union-drift] MUST-FIX finalize and check-phase-review-receipt.js use contradictory verdict semantics across generations: finalize aggregates only the current generation's findings (earlier verified Criticals are closed by absence, so the g2 receipt is SHIP-AS-IS — blessed by hetero-review-loop.test.sh case 7), while the checker's Mode A loop unions verified Criticals over EVERY finalized generation in receipt.chain and never reads the closed_findings records finalize writes — concrete failure: the intended remediation loop (g1 verified Critical → FIX-THEN-SHIP → fix → g2 clean) yields a receipt the gate rejects with "Receipt verdict mismatch: expected 'FIX-THEN-SHIP'", making any phase that ever had a verified Critical permanently unpassable (fail-closed availability break of the gate); the same drift hits open_findings (checker accumulates across generations, finalize writes current-generation only); no test feeds a multi-generation finalize receipt through the checker (e2e case 12 is single-generation), so this is undetected. Smallest remediation: in Mode A, skip an earlier-generation finding whose id appears in a later finalized generation's closed_findings (or aggregate only the last generation plus still-open earlier findings), and add one multi-generation e2e checker assertion.
🟠 [d2-checker-malformed-artifact-fail-open] MUST-FIX Mode A re-derivation coerces malformed artifacts to empty instead of failing closed: genFindings/genDispFindings use `Array.isArray(...) ? ... : []`, finding entries are not validated (severity must be in {Critical, Major, Minor, Suggestion}, id a non-empty string), and a non-array/non-number receipt.open_findings silently skips its check — concrete failure: after finalize, an implementer rewrites gN/findings.json to `{}` (or downcases a severity to "critical") and sets receipt.verdict to SHIP-AS-IS; re-derivation sees zero findings and the forged receipt exits 0, whereas finalize validates the very same files strictly (exit 1) — a fail-closed gap on malformed input and a format-strictness drift between the D2 scripts. Smallest remediation: mirror finalize's validation in Mode A (exit 1 unless findings.json/dispositions.json are objects with findings arrays, ids non-empty strings, severities in the four-word vocabulary, and receipt.open_findings an array).
🟡 [d1-hetero-auto-no-expansion] MUST-FIX the shipped contract row for `hetero_review` (project-config-template/review-loop-config.md, both canonical and mirrored copies) states `auto` ⇒ "tuple expanded from ~/.autopilot/topology.json", but the resolver's auto branch only sets hetero_review_resolved_from=topology and leaves reviewer_* untouched (resolve-review-loop.test.sh blesses "reviewer_engine is UNCHANGED") — concrete failure: an operator relying on the documented expansion keeps the config/native reviewer while the provenance field claims topology seating, a misleading trust signal for the loop consumers. Smallest remediation: either correct the hetero_review row/Gotcha to "provenance-only, reviewer_* unchanged" or expand reviewer_* from reviewer_ladder[0] mirroring the consult branch.
🔵 [d2-tests-bare-fs-node-e] CUT/FOLLOW-UP hetero-review-loop.test.sh (cases 4, 4-fin, 7, 7d, T1, T4) and check-phase-review-receipt.test.sh (case 12 FINDING_ID) invoke `node -e` with bare `fs`/`crypto` and no require while sibling sites in the same files require them explicitly; stock Node injects core modules only in the REPL, not `-e`, so if lib.sh does not shim node these sites throw ReferenceError and their assertions fail — excluded from this version because the committed ledgers record the exact suites green (69/69, 131/131, 20/20), implying an environment-provided preload; harden by adding `require('fs')`/`require('crypto')` for portability at next touch.
🔵 [d1-consult-alias-exclusion] CUT/FOLLOW-UP consult auto's qc-exclusion compares raw `engine|runner|effort` strings, so agy aliases (gemini-flash → gemini-3.6-flash-high) and codex-cli vs normalized codex never match the topology ladder and a qc seat can be picked as the consult seat (quality-pipeline's "resolver enforces this mechanically" claim is false in that case) — already documented as a BACKLOG row, advisory-only rail with no gate decision depending on it; normalise both sides when next touching the exclusion builder.
🔵 [d2-receipt-chain-not-diffed] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Mode A never compares receipt.chain to the on-disk chain.json beyond entry[0].base, so truncating an empty-diff generation from the receipt's chain could skip its findings in re-derivation — exploiting it requires an attacker-authored ledger that is visible in the committed diff and reviewed at depth-0; add a full receipt.chain ≡ chainOnDisk equality check as hardening.
🔵 [d2-modeb-duplicate-ids] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Mode B builds dispMap without a duplicate-id check (last entry wins), unlike finalize's strict duplicate rejection — plan-artifact inputs are depth-0-owned; add the dup check when Mode B is next touched.
